# Engineering Practice

How the scribl production app is built: the decisions behind it, the standards it
holds to, and the setup a developer needs.

The rest of this handbook is delivery process, meaning how work flows, how it is
estimated and when it is done. This section is engineering practice, meaning how
the code itself is structured, written, tested and secured.

## Read in this order

**Start here.**

- [Decision Register](decision-register.md) -- every architectural and
  engineering choice on the production build, with the reason for it and the
  trade-off it accepts. Shareable as-is with anyone who needs to understand or
  challenge a choice. If you read one page, read this one.

**How the code is organised and written.**

- [Architecture](architecture.md) -- the layers, what each may import, and the
  decision table for where a given piece of code goes. Every boundary in it is
  enforced by the pipeline rather than by review.
- [Service Seams](service-seams.md) -- how every external dependency is
  wrapped so replacing it is a day rather than a sprint: authentication,
  crash reporting, logging, media and notifications. Holds the rule for where
  a seam's swap point goes, the Cognito decisions including the one signature
  that keeps MFA cheap, the one-event-many-formatters logging design behind
  both plain-text support bundles and CloudWatch JSON, the shared diagnostics
  consent gate, what is deliberately not collected and what each absence buys,
  and the provider tree with the reasoning for each depth.
- [Engineering Standards](engineering-standards.md) -- coding standards, design
  principles stated with their failure modes, the testing tiers ranked by what
  they prevent, and mobile application security.

**How it is built and shipped.**

- [Toolchain](toolchain.md) -- the package manager decision and why, the tool
  set, the complete command surface, and the build variants for development, QA
  and production.
- [CI and CD](ci-cd.md) -- pipeline design, the constraint that shapes it, and
  the release path from a commit to a build in a tester's hands.
- [Release Readiness](release-readiness.md) -- what has to be true before a
  build reaches a tester and later a store: prerequisites, the required build
  artifacts, and the store requirements this app actually triggers.

**Working on it.**

- [Developer Setup](dev-setup.md) -- machine setup, what works on day one and
  what needs a prerequisite, verification and troubleshooting.
- [Developer Bootstrap Script](developer-bootstrap.md) -- the idempotent setup
  script, reproduced so it can be read without cloning.
- [Feature Flags](feature-flags.md) -- the flag seam, its typed registry, and
  the rules that are not negotiable.
- [Blocking Questions](code-questions.md) -- the questions that currently stop
  code being written, each with an owner and, where one exists, the architect's
  working position.

## This is the one copy

**This section is the source of truth for the Scribl production build's
engineering documentation.** Until 2026-08-27 these pages were published
copies of documents that lived beside their configuration in the
`scribl-mobile-app` code repository, kept in step by a publish script run from
that repo. That model is retired: going forward there is exactly one copy of
each page, held here.

**Why the change.** A copy that a script has to keep in step is a copy that can
drift, and the failure mode is a document that reads as current while being
wrong. One copy in one place cannot drift from itself.

**So edit these pages directly.** After a change, run `npm run docs:sync` from
this repository so the rendered site picks it up. There is no publish step and
nothing to run from `scribl-mobile-app`; the `publish-docs-to-brain.mjs` script and
the `docs:publish` / `docs:publish:check` commands in that repo are retired,
see `toolchain.md`.

**Update this page in the same unit of work as the change it documents.** This
is the same pairing rule this repo already applies to stories, for the same
reason: a document that disagrees with what shipped is worse than no document,
because it gets believed. A change in `scribl-mobile-app` that a page here
describes, an architecture boundary, a toolchain command, a CI step, still
needs that page updated here, in whatever commit or pull request lands the
change in this repository.

## What is deliberately not published here

The scaffold instruction used to generate the initial codebase stays in the code
repository. It is an instruction to a build agent rather than documentation, it
is consumed once, and it would read as guidance to a person if it appeared on
this site.

Anything still undecided that does not block code belongs on
[the open questions page](/open-questions), which is the engagement-wide
register. The blocking-questions page above is the code-side subset.
